## What this version has not answered

Nothing here is a negative result. These are questions the battery is ready to ask and
nobody has run yet on this version — which is the state a capability is in for as long as
it takes the game to grow it.

- `distribution.mcworld.carries_its_own_packs` — Does a `.mcworld` containing its own `behavior_packs/` and `resource_packs/` folders import with those packs active, without touching the global pack list?
  <br><sub>Import the released `.mcworld` WITHOUT installing the `.mcaddon` first -- ideally on a device where the pack is not installed at all. Join the world, then check three things: the world exists with the name it was published under, `/scriptevent bedshock:probe` gets a response in chat, and the global pack list in Settings does NOT list a new bedshock entry.</sub>
- `entity.container.reachable_slots_match_declared_size` — Can a player reach every slot the container declares, or only some of them?
- `equipment.offhand.vanilla_permitted_item_persists` — Does a vanilla item the off-hand normally accepts -- a shield -- stay there when a script puts it in?
- `equipment.offhand.ejected_item_survives` — When the client ejects a script-placed item from the off-hand, does the item still exist?
- `item.durability_bar.rows_covered` — Which pixel rows of the 16x16 icon does the durability bar's dark track cover?
  <br><sub>The ruler item in your hotbar. Every one of its 16 rows is a different colour and the bottom five are pure primaries, so you can count off which rows the bar eats. Two copies are given: one nearly pristine (long green bar) and one nearly spent (1px red). The dark track is full-width in both, and it is the track that occludes.</sub>
- `item.durability_bar.track_appears_at_damage_one` — Does the dark track appear at `damage == 1`, not just when the item is visibly worn?
  <br><sub>The nearly-pristine ruler copy (damage 1). Look for the dark track, not the fill.</sub>
- `item.icon.animates_from_flipbook` — Does an item atlas tile animate from a `flipbook_textures.json` entry?
  <br><sub>The two flipbook probe items in your hotbar. They carry the SAME animation under two deliberately different spellings -- one with explicit `frames: [0,1,2,3]` and `blend_frames: false`, one omitting `frames` with `blend_frames: true`. Different in every field that could plausibly be the mistake.</sub>
- `item.name.glyph_renders_in_item_name` — Does a glyph render in an ITEM's name and in the actionbar, not only in chat?
  <br><sub>The glyph probe item in your hotbar -- its nameTag carries all four rings -- and the actionbar line the probe prints. Compare both against the chat line.</sub>
- `item.creative.hidden_by_omitting_category` — Does omitting `menu_category` entirely hide an item from the creative menu?
  <br><sub>The creative menu. Six probe items are generated, each labelled in-game with which variant it is, so the picker screenshot is self-describing. Search for "P7".</sub>
- `item.creative.hidden_by_category_none` — Does an explicit `category: none` hide an item from the creative menu?
  <br><sub>The creative menu, searching for "P7 category none".</sub>
- `item.creative.custom_group_nests_items` — Does a shared custom `group` collapse several items into one expandable pile?
  <br><sub>The three items labelled "P7 grouped A/B/C", which share one group string.</sub>
- `item.creative.order_follows_emission` — Does the creative menu order items by the order their files are emitted?
  <br><sub>The order the six P7 items appear in. They are emitted in the order listed in the probe config -- omitted, none, items, grouped A, B, C.</sub>
- `item.dynamic_properties.survive_world_reload` — Do dynamic properties on an ItemStack survive a full quit to title and reload?
  <br><sub>Run `/scriptevent bedshock:probe dynprops.stamp`, then QUIT TO TITLE and reload the world, then run `/scriptevent bedshock:probe dynprops.token`. The probe stamps a per-load session token, so the readout can tell you outright whether a reload actually happened between the two halves -- a run made in one sitting reports itself as such rather than being mistaken for the real measurement.</sub>
- `item.durability.mending_can_reach_a_custom_item` — Does a Mending enchantment repair a custom item's `damage`?
  <br><sub>Put Mending on the probe durability item, note the damage the probe prints, collect XP, then run the probe again to re-read it.</sub>
- `item.durability.anvil_or_grindstone_can_reach_a_custom_item` — Can an anvil or a grindstone alter a custom item's `damage`?
  <br><sub>Take the probe durability item to an anvil, then to a grindstone. Does either offer to repair or strip it? If one does, take the offer and re-read the damage.</sub>
- `item.durability.omitting_repairable_blocks_external_writes` — Is omitting `minecraft:repairable` enough to keep anvils, grindstones and Mending away from an item's damage?
  <br><sub>The probe items declare no `minecraft:repairable` -- deliberately, so this is testable at all. Answer this only after reading the two rows above.</sub>
- `item.durability.ordinary_use_consumes_it` — Does using a custom item consume durability the way a tool's does?
  <br><sub>The probe durability item's damage, before and after using it twenty times.</sub>
- `physics.knockback.blocks_per_unit` — How far does one unit of `applyKnockback` actually move a player?
- `render.attachable.several_controllers_at_once` — Can several render controllers run on one attachable simultaneously?
  <br><sub>How many of the four flags draw at once, and whether there is any z-fighting or ordering artefact between them.</sub>
- `render.attachable.accepts_vanilla_hold_animations` — Will a custom item's attachable accept the vanilla hold animations and be posed into the hand?
  <br><sub>A separate rig carrying `animations` plus a `scripts.animate` list selecting on `c.is_first_person`, copied from the vanilla resource pack's own attachables. Hold it and check both persons. Do NOT fold this into the flag rig -- posing those flags into the hand would make them small and half-occluded, which is the exact failure that rig has already been repaired for twice.</sub>
- `ui.form.button_icon_resolves_an_unindexed_path` — Does `ActionFormData.button(text, iconPath)` draw a texture that has NO `item_texture.json` entry?
  <br><sub>Button 1 in the form the probe opens. Its texture is written to `textures/probe/` and deliberately LEFT OUT of `item_texture.json` -- its absence there is the exact thing being ruled out. Button 2 is a vanilla path and is the control: if IT does not draw, the mechanism is broken and button 1 means nothing.</sub>
- `ui.form.button_icon_resolves_a_bare_atlas_key` — Does a bare atlas short-name work where a path is expected?
  <br><sub>Button 3, which passes a bare atlas key rather than a path. Expected to fail.</sub>
- `ui.form.missing_icon_is_visually_distinct` — Does a deliberately wrong icon path render as a broken-texture mark, or as nothing?
  <br><sub>Button 4, which points at a path that deliberately does not exist.</sub>

## Settled without a probe

Established well enough not to spend a battery slot on — by reading what the engine does, or
by an API that does not exist. Recorded so nobody re-derives them, and so a future
contradiction is visible as a contradiction.

| Claim | Established by | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Does importing an `.mcaddon` whose UUID is already installed replace the installed copy? | Observed repeatedly on iPadOS across more than a hundred installs: the import is refused as a DUPLICATE rather than replacing anything. The old copy has to be uninstalled first, and the client caches the pack list hard enough that the app must be closed before the new copy is offered. Only marketplace content updates in place. Recorded as `derived` rather than measured because it is not reachable from inside a pack: no script API touches the content manager. It is a property of the client, established by somebody paying for it a hundred times. | Whether iterating on an add-on is cheap or expensive, and therefore how much a single in-game session has to accomplish. If a rebuild costs one import, a session can be casual and repeated. If it costs an uninstall, an app restart and a world rebuild, then every session has to be one-pass, resumable in place, and worth the setup -- which is a hard constraint on the guided run rather than a preference. |
| Can a custom BLOCK carry a container, or must it be an entity? | Blocks cannot be containers on Bedrock; only entities carry `minecraft:inventory`. | Whether custom storage costs an entity -- with everything that implies about collision, persistence and chunk loading -- or can be a block like a chest. |
| Is a custom entity solid to a player, given `minecraft:collision_box` and `minecraft:physics` with `has_collision: true`? | Measured in play on two separate custom entities: you walk through them. `collision_box` governs hit detection and entity-entity pushing, not player blocking. | Whether anything that must be walked AROUND can be an entity, or needs a real block. |
| Can another entity stand on a custom entity? | Measured: a dropped anvil passes through a custom entity and lands in its cell. The other half of the same fact as the player row above. | Whether an entity can serve as a platform or a landing target. |
| Can a player put an arbitrary item in the off-hand by hand? | The off-hand only accepts items whose definition permits it. This is vanilla behaviour and is what rules out "put anything in your off-hand, then open the menu" as an input gesture. | Whether the off-hand can be an INPUT -- somewhere a player deliberately puts something for a pack to notice. |
| Is there an off-hand use input on any Bedrock platform? | Bedrock has no off-hand use input on any platform. | Whether an off-hand item can be interactive, or is inert decoration. Inert suits a decoration; it rules out anything that wanted to be a second tool. |
| Can two stacks of the same item type draw different inventory icons? | `minecraft:icon` is static per item type and Bedrock has no damage-based icon selection; that is a Java-only feature. There is nothing resembling `CustomModelData`. | Everything about how much state an item can show. If no, every distinguishable visual configuration costs one item type, and any item that changes state constantly must NOT encode that state in its type -- because a type swap is a remove-and-give, and that is the mechanism by which stack data gets silently dropped. |
| Can an icon be tinted or composited at runtime, at any layer? | No runtime tint or sprite-overlay API exists for item icons on Bedrock. Colour has to be in the texture, which means in the item type. | Whether a colour axis can be applied at render time or has to be baked. Baking is what turns 3 dimensions x 16 colours into 48 sprites instead of 19. |
| Do dynamic properties require an item with `max_stack_size: 1`? | Per-stack state cannot survive stacks merging, and Bedrock's API reflects that. Already relied on in generated item definitions. | A real inventory cost, paid deliberately by every item that carries state. Worth knowing before designing something that wanted to be stackable. |
| Does an unrecognised Molang query resolve to 0 rather than erroring? | Read off the engine's behaviour across several controller failures. An unresolvable query for an ENTITY property additionally fails the whole render controller silently, which is a different and worse failure -- four sessions were lost to it before the query was found to be `query.property` rather than `query.actor_property`. | How every other probe in this file has to be read. If an unknown query silently yields 0, then a controller indexing a texture array with a dead query still draws -- it draws index 0. So index 0 is the signal for "this query is blind", and no probe expectation may land on index 0 except the one that expects zero anyway. Getting this backwards makes every rendering measurement unreadable. |
| Does Molang's float arithmetic stay exact across a bit-packed integer layout? | Molang is float-based; integers stay exact well past 2^24, which is far above any packed layout worth designing. Use power-of-two bases for readability. | Whether `math.floor` and `math.mod` can safely unpack a value carried in durability or any other numeric channel. |
| Does an attachable with no `animations` and no `scripts.animate` render at the player model's own origin? | Read directly out of the attachable JSON we emit: it declares only `materials`, `textures`, `geometry` and `render_controllers`. With nothing switching poses, the model renders in the player model's coordinate space at its origin and stays there in both first and third person. Confirmed against play reports of the probe appearing behind the player, which is where its authored offset puts it. | Whether "it appeared on my back" is a property of attachables or a property of our geometry offsets. The answer changes whether a hand pose needs work or just needs coordinates. |
| Can script open a container UI for a player without the player interacting? | There is no `player.openContainer` in the script API. | Whether a container screen can be part of a scripted flow, or is always something the player has to reach for themselves. |
| Is there an event for a container's contents changing? | No container-change event exists; contents must be polled. | Whether watching a container costs a poll. Cheap for one open container; a real cost if a design wants many. |
| Can custom enchantments be defined, or the enchanting-table UI intercepted? | Custom enchantments cannot be defined and the enchanting-table UI cannot be intercepted. The glint still requires a real vanilla enchantment. | Whether the enchanting table is a route to a custom "attach"-style interaction. It is a tempting one because the UI already exists and reads as native. |
| Is there an API to resolve an item id to the texture path that draws it? | Form button `iconPath` is a texture path rather than an item id, and no runtime API maps one to the other. Our own art is unaffected because we control those paths. | Whether a UI can draw an ARBITRARY item -- including one from another pack. Without it, anything that wants to needs a generated id-to-path table plus a placeholder for everything unrecognised. |
